content: The Journal of Experimental Medicine is an academic publication dedicated to disseminating research papers and commentaries within the field of biomedical science. The journal focuses on a range of topics, including immunology, inflammation, infectious diseases, hematopoiesis, cancer, stem cell biology, and vascular biology. Historically, the journal has primarily published basic research. However, studies involving human subjects have been increasingly represented, accounting for approximately 10% of the published papers as of 2004. The Journal of Experimental Medicine was established in 1896, making it one of the longest-running scientific journals in existence. Initially published at Johns Hopkins University, the journal was taken over in 1905 by the Rockefeller University Press, which continues to publish it on a not-for-profit basis. The journal does not have a single Editor-in-Chief. Instead, it is managed by a team of eleven academic editors and supported by an advisory board comprising over one hundred members. The journal is published on a monthly basis. An online archive of articles dating back to 1896 is available in both text and PDF formats. However, material from 1996 and earlier is only accessible in PDF format. Articles older than six months are freely accessible, and all papers are made available free of charge to developing countries. The Journal of Experimental Medicine is recognized as one of the leading biomedical journals, with a significant impact in the field.
